unit.title: Living Things
unit.blurb: What is alive? Plants and animals grow, need food and water, and make new living things. The parts of a plant.
unit.subject: science

O1.t: Tell the difference between things that are alive and things that are not.

O2.t: Name the parts of a plant: root, stem, leaf and flower.

p: A dog is **alive**. It eats, drinks, breathes, moves and grows bigger. One day it can have puppies.
A rock is **not alive**. It does not eat, it does not grow and it cannot make baby rocks.
A plant cannot walk, but it is still **alive**. It grows, it needs water and light, and it makes seeds that grow into new plants.
Does it grow? Does it need food or water? Can it make new living things? If the answer is yes, it is alive.
A car moves, but it is not alive: it does not grow or eat. A tree does not walk, but it is alive.

p: The **roots** grow under the soil and take in water. The **stem** holds the plant up. The **leaves** use sunlight to make food. The **flower** makes seeds.

lesson.t: Why does a plant need roots?
lesson.q: If you pull up a plant, what do you see at the bottom?
steps: they spread out in the soil
and hold the plant in the ground
lesson.a: Roots drink water and hold the plant still.

lesson.t: Not every plant has big flowers
p: Grass is a plant too, with tiny flowers. Look for roots, a stem and leaves.
